questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the past perfect tense?
options: She said she _____ to London before she moved there.
She said she _____ to London before she moved there.
She said she _____ to London before she moved there.
She said she _____ to London before she moved there.
questions.answer: She said she had been to London before she moved there.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence with the present perfect tense.
options: I _____ never seen that film.
I never _____ seen that film.
I never seen that film.
I never seen that film.
questions.answer: I have never seen that film.

questions.question: Which option correctly compares two things using comparatives?
options: This book is more interesting than that one.
This book is more interesting than that one.
This book is more interesting than that one.
This book is more interesting than that one.
questions.answer: This book is more interesting than that one.

questions.question: Select the correct conditional sentence type 3.
options: If I had known, I would have helped you.
If I had known, I would have helped you.
If I had known, I would have helped you.
If I had known, I would have helped you.
questions.answer: If I had known, I would have helped you.

questions.question: Which modal verb is used to give advice?
options: You should go to the doctor.
You could go to the doctor.
You might go to the doctor.
You must go to the doctor.
questions.answer: You should go to the doctor.

questions.question: Choose the correct form after 'remember to' + verb.
options: I remember to post the letter.
I remember to post the letter.
I remember to post the letter.
I remember to post the letter.
questions.answer: I remember to post the letter.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the gerund correctly?
options: I enjoy swimming in the sea.
I enjoy swimming in the sea.
I enjoy swimming in the sea.
I enjoy swimming in the sea.
questions.answer: I enjoy swimming in the sea.

questions.question: Select the correct infinitive form after 'decide to' + verb.
options: She decided to go to the party.
She decided to go to the party.
She decided to go to the party.
She decided to go to the party.
questions.answer: She decided to go to the party.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the conjunction 'although'?
options: Although it was raining, they played football.
Although it was raining, they played football.
Although it was raining, they played football.
Although it was raining, they played football.
questions.answer: Although it was raining, they played football.

questions.question: Choose the word that best fits the context of a B1-level vocabulary question.
options: He was very _____ about his work.
He was very _____ about his work.
He was very _____ about his work.
He was very _____ about his work.
questions.answer: He was very particular about his work.
